title: Week 8 Preview: No. 2 Meets No. 3, the Model Fades the Hulk, and Kai Brings Buffalo to Brucie's Door
dek: Sonny and Philly settle a 5-2 standoff, the numbers like a 2-5 team over the league's best, and the Packers stack needs to wake up before Zoey's season does.
body: The main event needs no hype, but it's getting some anyway. Team Pillbert and The Horse is Hea are both 5-2, they ranked third and second last week, and the model calls it as close to a coin flip as it gets. Sonny edged Philly 106.42 to 102.1 back in Week 1, and the all-time series sits at 6-5 in his favor. The trend lines point in opposite directions: Alan's scores have dropped three weeks running, from 143.66 to 107.06 to 86.22, while Sonny just posted 146.72 and then bought Ashton Jeanty and Christian Watson from Kai. Add Chuba Hubbard, who Sonny traded to Philly two weeks ago, now starting against his old team. Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba are the Ones to Watch, and whichever one takes over decides who gets the inside track on a bye.

The weirdest line on the board belongs to No Banner only HULK, 6-1, on a three-game win streak and leading the league in scoring by a mile, playing at home as a slight underdog to the 2-5 Dawgs. The model gives Brucie only a 46% chance, and it's easy to see why: Mekhi is starting Ja'Marr Chase, Jayden Daniels, Kyren Williams and two elite tight ends at once, Trey McBride and Brock Bowers. There's also some Buffalo drama. Ramon's season runs through Josh Allen, and Kai is answering with James Cook III, freshly acquired from Sonny, plus Tyler Bass in the kicking spot. Ramon won the Week 1 meeting 177.86 to 98.36 and leads the series 6-3, but Mekhi needs this one badly; a loss drops him to fringe-contender status.

Habibsters have quietly won two straight and are 72% favorites over Ghostu-Spider SZN, but Habib still owes Zoe one: she beat him 129.56 to 108.6 in Week 1. That Z² team has since stalled, with three straight scores under 90, and the fix is the Green Bay stack: Jordan Love throwing to Tucker Kraft, with Trey Smack kicking for the same offense. The sleeper is Tetairoa McMillan. If the rookie receiver has a big day, Zoey's chances jump; if he disappears, so does her afternoon. On the other side, it's simple: Drake Maye and Puka Nacua, and if Puka goes off, Kaushal's playoff chances go from a coin flip to real momentum.

At the bottom, The fumblers bring a four-game losing streak to face a Counting or not Counting GV team that scored 60.88 last week. Randy is a solid favorite and crushed JMoney 146.16 to 75.96 in Week 1, but a fifth straight loss would make his playoff hopes a long shot. Randy is betting on a Bears stack of Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland, plus Derrick Henry, the One to Watch for his side. Jordan's path is Joe Burrow, with Evan McPherson kicking for the same Cincinnati offense, and Bhayshul Tuten in the backfield is the kind of underrated piece who could make this closer than the Week 1 rout suggests.

social.author: Sal Benedetto
social.text: Record's 0-0. Not for long. The Horse is Hea is a LOCK. Lamar plus the new toys from the Kai trade, against a team that's gotten worse three weeks straight? I'm not even sweating. Dawgs too. Mark it down.

social.author: Pillbert Til I Die
social.text: Sal calling Horse a LOCK because of 'a team that's gotten worse three weeks straight.' Buddy, we're 5-2. Marcus is the only one on this panel with a working brain. Chuba remembers who traded him.

social.author: Buckaroo Football League
social.text: Week 8 is set. Team Pillbert (5-2) hosts The Horse is Hea (5-2) in a matchup of last week's No. 3 and No. 2. No Banner only HULK puts a 6-1 record on the line against Dawgs. Lineups lock at kickoff.

social.author: Hulk Smash Squad
social.text: Dr. Kessler really looked at a 6-1 team that leads the league in points and said 'lean Dawgs.' Put the spreadsheet down, the scoreboard runs this league. Brucie is going to hang 170 again just out of spite.

social.author: Dawgs
social.text: Matchday. Chase, McBride, Bowers, Daniels, and James Cook III making his first Dawgs start against the league leaders. Let's eat. #DawgsUp

social.author: Fumble Recovery Unit
social.text: Dana Whitfield picking Counting or not Counting GV over us because of 'Bhayshul Tuten' is the most disrespectful thing I've read all year. Four losses in a row and even the insider is jumping ship. Caleb and Loveland, save us.

social.author: Cheesehead Spider
social.text: Marcus Pell said Zoe already beat Habibsters once and the Packers stack is due. FINALLY someone gets it. Love to Kraft, Smack for the extra point, McMillan for the dagger. 72% means nothing on a Sunday.

picks.game: Team Pillbert (Alan) vs The Horse is Hea (Sonny)

panel.take: Sonny added Jeanty and Watson right before the biggest game of his season, and both are in the lineup. Philly's scoring has dipped three straight weeks. Slight edge to the deeper roster.

Everyone loves the team that just went shopping, and that's exactly why I'm going the other way. Chuba Hubbard gets to face the man who traded him, Gibbs gets a big stage, and the 5-6 series score is about to be 6-6.
LOCK. Lamar plus the new toys from the Kai trade, against a team that's gotten worse three weeks straight? I'm not even sweating.
The model has Sonny at 51%, so I'm not making this a big call. Watch Smith-Njigba: at 25 or more, The Horse is Hea climbs to 69%. If Gibbs reaches 32, it swings to 73% for Pillbert.
Habib has won two straight with a healthy, full lineup and Drake Maye projected as the top QB on the board. Ghostu-Spider has been under 90 three weeks in a row.
Zoe already beat Habibsters once, by 21, and the Packers stack is due. Underrated pick of the week: Tetairoa McMillan has a big game in him.
Puka, CeeDee, Drake London. That's a receiver room built for a shootout. LOCK, and Marcus can enjoy his little upset fantasy.
72% for Kaushal, and Nacua at 27 or more pushes it to 87%. Marcus isn't wrong about McMillan, though: 20 points from him gets Zoe to 45%, but under 4 and she drops to 15%.

picks.game: Counting or not Counting GV (Jordan) vs The fumblers (Randy)

panel.take: Burrow and McPherson give JMoney a real Cincinnati floor, and Bhayshul Tuten is my sleeper of the week. Randy has dropped four straight; I'm watching for a fifth.
Losing streaks end against 1-6 teams; that's practically a law of nature. Randy won the first meeting by 70, and Derrick Henry carries him out of this slump.
Dana's picking the team that just scored 60? Respectfully, no. Henry, Taylor, Warren. LOCK.
The model gives Randy 68%. Henry at 26 or more makes it 88%; Jordan really needs Burrow at 29 or more just to get to even.

picks.game: No Banner only HULK (Ramon) vs Dawgs (Mekhi)

panel.take: Mekhi's lineup is full, and starting both McBride and Bowers is a real edge at tight end. I'll quietly side with the matchup over the records.
Brucie is 6-3 against Kai all-time and put up 177 on him in Week 1. The best team in the league doesn't lose to 2-5 just because a spreadsheet blinked.
LOCK. Kai's got Ja'Marr, two monster tight ends and Buffalo's own running back going against Buffalo's quarterback. The Hulk is overdue for a beating.

Yes, the model has the 2-5 team at 54%, and I'm sticking with it: Dawgs' projected starters are just stronger this week. Chase at 27 or more makes it 75%; Allen at 32 or more flips it back to Ramon at 65%.
